skill.name: security-engineer
skill.description: Guides authorized security assessments across penetration testing, secure code review, vulnerability management, monitoring, incident response, hardening, and compliance.
skill.summary: Plan, perform, and document authorized security reviews with practical workflows and established tools.
skill.author: zl2023github

security_audit.summary: Most critical static alerts are false positives caused by defensive examples, public references, and Markdown syntax. Actionable scanning, sensitive-data inspection, destructive removal, and an unaudited hidden-path script remain confirmed risks. The broad post-exploitation workflow creates additional high dual-use risk despite its authorization reminder.

remediation.issue: The workflow includes exploitation, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and brute-force activity.
remediation.suggestion: Require written scope, target allowlisting, and separate user confirmation before each active or post-exploitation action. Remove lateral movement and brute-force guidance from default workflows.

remediation.issue: The ClamAV example recursively deletes detected files with --remove.
remediation.suggestion: Replace deletion with quarantine and require review before any removal. State the affected path and backup status before execution.

remediation.issue: The PDF guide executes a generator from an unaudited hidden home-directory path.
remediation.suggestion: Package the generator with the skill, reference it by a package-relative path, and verify its integrity before execution.

remediation.issue: Several scanner and forensic commands can affect targets or expose sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Add per-command impact notes, least-impact defaults, secret redaction, bounded paths, and explicit confirmation before execution.

content.value_statement: Security reviews require consistent scope, evidence, and remediation guidance across many tools. This skill provides practical workflows for authorized assessment, monitoring, hardening, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Plans authorized security assessments for applications, APIs, infrastructure, cloud environments, containers, and mobile applications.
Recommends established tools for asset discovery, active scanning, source review, dependency review, and configuration auditing.
Provides checklists for Web security, authentication, data protection, and infrastructure controls.
Guides alert triage, forensic analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and incident review.
Produces structured findings with severity, evidence, reproduction steps, impact, and remediation guidance.
Maps common vulnerabilities to detection methods and defensive controls.
limitations: It does not verify that a target owner granted authorization.
Tool availability, versions, permissions, and operating system differences can change command behavior.
Automated scanner results still require manual validation and context-specific risk assessment.
Some workflows and commands can disrupt services, expose sensitive data, or delete files.

use_cases.title: Review Application Security
use_cases.description: Assess code and application behavior, validate scanner findings, and prepare prioritized remediation guidance.

use_cases.title: Build DevSecOps Controls
use_cases.description: Select source, dependency, container, and configuration checks for a controlled delivery pipeline.

use_cases.title: Investigate Security Alerts
use_cases.description: Organize triage, evidence collection, containment, recovery, and post-incident reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Security Review Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized security review plan for [system]. Define scope, assumptions, evidence, low-impact checks, approval gates, and report sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a bounded assessment

prompt_templates.title: Review Source Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [repository or files] for injection, access control, secret handling, unsafe uploads, SSRF, XXE, and deserialization risks. Explain evidence and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a DevSecOps Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design security checks for [stack and pipeline]. Include SAST, dependency, secret, container, and configuration scanning with validation and release criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Lead an Incident Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an incident workflow for [alert and environment]. Prioritize preservation, triage, containment, forensic questions, recovery criteria, communication, and lessons learned.

output_examples.input: Assess an internal API after written authorization and provide a review plan.
output: Scope: the approved API hosts, accounts, methods, and testing window.
Sequence: passive review, low-impact validation, approved active checks, manual confirmation, and reporting.
Evidence: timestamps, affected endpoints, sanitized requests, observed impact, and tool versions.
Stop conditions: unexpected service degradation, scope uncertainty, or sensitive data exposure.

output_examples.input: Summarize a confirmed broken access control issue for an engineering team.
output_examples.output: High severity: a standard user can access another account record by changing its identifier. Enforce server-side ownership checks and add negative authorization tests.

output_examples.input: Prepare an incident response checklist for suspicious authentication activity.
output: Validate the alert source, affected identities, time range, and authentication method.
Preserve relevant identity, application, endpoint, and network evidence.
Contain confirmed abuse while protecting evidence and required business access.
Document recovery criteria, monitoring changes, owners, and follow-up actions.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, exact targets, timing, and stop conditions before active testing.
Use least-impact checks first and request separate approval before exploitation or destructive actions.
Redact sensitive evidence, validate automated findings manually, and record reproducible remediation steps.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public or third-party targets without verified authorization.
Do not run destructive flags or broad filesystem commands without backups, bounded paths, and confirmation.
Do not report scanner output as confirmed vulnerabilities without manual evidence and impact analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill perform penetration testing automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and commands. Execution depends on available tools, permissions, user approval, and a verified authorized scope.

faq.question: Can it review source code?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers automated and manual review for common injection, authentication, access control, data exposure, and file handling risks.

faq.question: Does it replace a security professional?
faq.answer: No. Qualified reviewers must validate authorization, business impact, tool output, legal requirements, and remediation decisions.

faq.question: Can it support incident response?
faq.answer: Yes. It structures triage, evidence collection, containment, eradication, recovery, monitoring, and retrospective analysis.

faq.question: Which security standards does it reference?
faq.answer: It references CVSS, OWASP, CVE, MITRE ATT&CK, CIS Benchmarks, and common compliance auditing practices.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the authorized scope, environment, target type, testing window, constraints, available tools, evidence rules, and expected report format.
